title: Comparison pullbacks of injective left-module sheaves are acyclic for arbitrary rings
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Lambda$ a discrete associative unital ring, not assumed commutative, in the coefficient universe. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in a common larger universe in which their underlying categories are small. A $\Lambda$-module sheaf means a sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules; equivalently it is a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant sheaf of rings, the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $
u_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}	o X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On module sheaves, $
u_X^*$ applies its set inverse image to addition, zero, negation and each scalar endomorphism of the underlying abelian sheaf; $
u_{X,*}$ is restriction to the étale subsite, with its induced scalar actions. Compute $R^q
u_{X,*}$ by injective resolutions in these module categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then for every injective left $\Lambda$-module sheaf $I$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and every integer $q>0$,
$$
R^q
u_{X,*}(
u_X^*I)=0.
$$
No affineness, quasi-compactness, torsion or finite-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution R of nu_X^* I in A-valued pro-etale sheaves. For each q, R.isoRightDerivedObj identifies the positive comparison direct image with homology of nu_X,* R. Restrict its degree-(q+1) short complex along AffineEtale.Spec X. This restriction is faithful and exact because the affine etale site is a dense subsite. It therefore suffices to show exactness after this restriction.

For W in X.AffineEtale, let T be its pro-etale image. Its structure morphism is etale and its source affine. Etale.injective_upperStar_obj_of_etale′ sends I to an injective on T.left_et. Apply stage3-affine-comparison-injective-derived-vanishing to this injective. The canonical adjunction conjugate comparisonUpperStarUpperStarIso identifies the resulting sheaf with the pro-etale pullback of nu_X^* I. Restriction to the localization T.left_proet is exact and preserves injectives. Evaluation of that restriction at the identity of T.left is naturally evaluation at T, via Over.isoMk (Iso.refl _). Transport this natural isomorphism through rightDerived and apply Functor.rightDerivedCompIsoOfExact. The result is vanishing of positive derived evaluation at T on X_proet. This entire localization calculation is the proved private helper affine_etale_sections_vanishing.

R.isoRightDerivedObj for evaluation turns step 2 into exactness of the evaluated short complex at every affine etale object. These are definitionally the evaluations of the underlying presheaf of the restriction in step 1. ShortComplex.exact_iff_evaluation gives presheaf exactness. Exact sheafification preserves it; ShortComplex.mapNatIso with sheafificationNatIso identifies the sheafified complex with the restricted sheaf complex. Finally faithful exact restriction reflects exactness, so the original homology is zero for each q. No assertion identifies sections of a higher direct-image sheaf with derived sections.

lean.note: Existing generic coefficient theorem, read in the source and in current server source via scompile.py --source. Specialize its ambient A to ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ with Λ : Type (u + 1) and [Ring Λ]. Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.AB supplies IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} with no commutativity or finiteness assumption; all required instances and the exact specialization were checked with scompile.py. Sheaf-valued left modules are the first, fixed-scalar encoding explicitly allowed in the node. The upstream comparison functors are restriction and canonical left Kan extension followed by sheafification, the same constructions as the recorded geometric comparison. Functor.rightAcyclic unfolds to every positive rightDerived degree. The stored signature is verbatim; A and its categorical instances are the surrounding variables in that source module. No duplicate module is delivered.
